book.fts_feelthenature.lookout_log.name: Lookout's Log
book.fts_feelthenature.lookout_log.cover:
FIRE LOOKOUT

Keep watch for smoke. Read the weather at the terminal morning and evening and log it here.

Lost or hurt? Call on the rescue frequency, 145.500 MHz.
book.fts_feelthenature.lookout_log.last: Whoever comes after: keep the stove going, the glass clean, and the log written.
book.fts_feelthenature.lookout_log.entry:
Day %s.

Clear morning, wind light from the west. No smoke seen.

Day %s.

Low cloud in the valley until noon. The peaks stood out of it like islands.

Day %s.

Thunder to the south in the afternoon. Watched where it struck until dark. Nothing caught.

Day %s.

Rain all day. The barometer climbing by evening.

Day %s.

A thin smoke to the north-east at dusk. A camp, I think. Will look again at first light.

Day %s.

Yesterday's smoke is gone. A campfire, not the forest.

Day %s.

Strong gusts. The anemometer on the roof sang all night.

Day %s.

Two walkers came up the stair and signed the book. They had lost the path by the river.

Day %s.

Frost on the rail at dawn. Wood for the stove running low.

Day %s.

A week clear and dry now. Fire danger high.

Day %s.

On the radio: a party overdue on the ridge. Kept the glass on it until dark.

Day %s.

Mist rising off the lake at sunrise. A heron at the shore.

Day %s.

Lightning on the rod in the night. All well.

Day %s.

Snow on the far peaks this morning. The season is turning.

Day %s.

Mended the third landing of the stair; a plank had split.

Day %s.

Calm. Read the old entries. Nothing to report but the view.
